name: Solberg-Maru Fab Floor Technician's Rig
description:
The standard working dress of a mid-level fabrication floor technician at a Solberg-Maru manufacturing plant — one of the major Circuit employers running continuous production lines in GLMZ's industrial eastern sectors. The centerpiece is a fitted coverall in deep charcoal grey synth-twill, single-piece construction with a heavy-gauge front zipper that runs from the left hip to the right shoulder in a diagonal — an ergonomic design that allows one-handed donning. The coverall has Solberg-Maru's angular teal-and-silver logo on the left chest and a name patch on the right reading in block letters. Sleeves are cut with extra fabric through the forearm for chrome arm accommodation and feature a secondary snap-seam from elbow to wrist that opens flat for workers with full prosthetic forearms. The back has a structured panel over the spine with magnetic attachment points for light exo-assist harness rigging. Knee pads are built-in hard-shell inserts with a quick-eject button on the outer knee.

Underneath the coverall, a long-sleeved moisture-wicking turtleneck in matte black keeps the neck and wrists protected from particulate. Safety boots are Solberg-Maru plant-standard: a matte charcoal composite-toe boot with a low heel, ESD-rated soles to prevent static discharge near sensitive fabrication equipment, and a wide-mouth tongue for easy on/off. The technician carries a tool belt worn over the coverall's exterior, a heavy nylon strap with modular snap-clip tool loops holding hex drivers, a calibration stylus, and a small diagnostic tablet in a rubberized holster. Safety glasses with teal-tinted lenses are pushed up on the forehead. Hair, if present, is tucked under a low-profile teal bump cap with the Solberg-Maru mark.
functionality: Diagonal zipper for one-handed donning; snap-open forearm seam for chrome arm accommodation; spinal magnetic attachment points for exo-assist harness; ESD-rated boot soles for fabrication environments; built-in quick-eject knee pads; modular tool belt with snap-clip loops; turtleneck particulate barrier at neck and wrists
what_it_says: Solberg-Maru plant workers occupy a specific Circuit niche: they're not scraping by, but they're not moving up either. The well-maintained coverall with its factory logo signals steady employment and plant loyalty. A technician who keeps their kit clean is someone who takes their work seriously — or someone who can't afford to lose this job. The chrome-accommodation seams say augmentation isn't unusual here; it's standard.
manufacturer: Solberg-Maru Industries (corponation-issued; manufactured in-house by Solberg-Maru Apparel Division)
price_range: Φ160–Φ220 (issued on hire; replacement at cost docked from wages)
story_hooks: A fabrication technician's coverall contains a hidden internal pocket sewn shut from the inside — and when it's finally cut open, it holds a data chip that shouldn't exist, encoded with Solberg-Maru production schematics for a product line the company hasn't officially announced.

A run of new coveralls issued to the night shift has a subtle difference in the snap-seam chrome accommodation — it's slightly misaligned in a way that could catch and damage a prosthetic limb under high-torque conditions, and someone changed the manufacturing spec deliberately.
The Solberg-Maru bump caps issued this quarter have an undocumented chip embedded in the brim — workers wearing them have been reporting fragmented memory intrusions near the BCI integration zones.

physical_description.visual_profile: A utilitarian one-piece coverall silhouette with bold diagonal front closure, suggesting industrial competence and mid-tier corporate identity. The teal-and-silver branding and structured back panel read as functional, purpose-built engineering wear rather than fashion. On the wearer, it projects pragmatic efficiency—a body prepared for machinery interaction.
physical_description.fit: Fitted through the torso with strategic extra volume at forearms and thighs. Compression-adjacent without being restrictive. The diagonal hip-to-shoulder zipper creates a dynamic visual line that emphasizes asymmetric movement capability. Sleeves accommodate prosthetic forearms without bunching.
physical_description.primary_material: Deep charcoal grey synth-twill (main coverall); matte black moisture-wicking turtleneck (base layer); matte charcoal composite-toe boot with ESD-rated sole
physical_description.texture: Smooth, industrial-grade synthetic twill with slight sheen under factory lighting. Turtleneck has a fine ribbed texture. Knee pad hard-shell inserts read as glossy polymer. Boot leather is treated composite—durable and scuff-resistant.
physical_description.color_scheme: Dominant charcoal grey coverall with teal-and-silver angular Solberg-Maru logo on left chest. Matte black turtleneck base. Teal-tinted safety glasses. Teal bump cap. Minimal accent color—the teal acts as corporate identifier and brand consistency.
physical_description.closures: Heavy-gauge diagonal front zipper (hip to right shoulder, one-handed operation). Secondary snap-seam elbow-to-wrist for prosthetic accommodation. Magnetic attachment points on spine panel for exo-assist harness. Quick-eject knee pad buttons.
distinctive_features: Solberg-Maru teal-and-silver angular logo on left chest
Block-letter name patch on right chest
Forearm expansion panels for chrome augmentation fit
Snap-seam elbow-to-wrist for full prosthetic forearms
Structured magnetic spine panel for exo-assist rigging
Built-in hard-shell knee pads with quick-eject buttons
Wide-mouth composite-toe boot tongue for accessibility
Modular tool belt with snap-clip loops
Teal bump cap with corporate branding
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 2–3 boundary: Corporation-issued manufacturing wear signaling employed mid-tier status and steady Circuit income. The fit and materials suggest functional quality rather than luxury, but the brand ownership and integrated augmentation accommodation mark this as legitimate corpo employee dress, not street salvage.
physical_description.cultural_context: Solberg-Maru manufacturing floor identity. Wearer is factory-bound, production-line embedded, augmentation-ready, and corporate-loyal. The uniform communicates reliability, technical competence, and acceptance of industrial hierarchy. Safety-first ethos. Suggests someone with semi-stable income, access to corpo healthcare, and compliance with plant protocols.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine to well-maintained when fresh from the plant. With regular wear, shows minor abrasion on knee pads, possible small oil stains or synthetic residue on cuffs and lower forearms, scuffing on boot toes. The zipper remains functional but may show dust accumulation. Overall: clean-professional with honest wear marks that signal active duty.
